newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - Klima says CA to go to top bid.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Klima says CA to go to top bid.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Tuesday a decision on the sale of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein would come as soon as possible and he would accept only the highest offer.
"It will happen as soon as possible," he told a news conference, adding: "I will accept the best and highest offer."
Klima last week extended the tender to January 10 from a previous deadline of December 16 to allow the current three bidders to boost their offers for Austria's blue-blooded bank.
"I will scrutinise the offers after they've landed on my desk at 9.00 (0800 GMT) on January 10 and I'm prepared to accept any offer that comes in above 16.7 billion schillings," he said.
Bank Austria has bid 16.8 billion schillings ($1.5 billion) for the government's 70 percent voting stake in conservative stronghold Creditanstalt.
Social Democrat Chancellor Franz Vranitzky on Monday said that the bank must be sold to the highest bidder, believed to be Bank Austria, in accordance with European Union law.

A rival consortium of bidders led by insurer EA-Generali has offered a total of 13.8 billion schillings for the state's 19.9 million shares in the bank and wants to sell about a quarter of those on the market at a premium, 60 percent of which would also go to the government's coffers.
The value of a third offer made by Austrian entrepreneur and former retail magnate Karl Wlaschek has not been disclosed but is estimated at around 15 billion schillings.

Vranitzky's Social Democrats (SPOe) back Bank Austria, controlled by the SPOe-dominated City of Vienna, while the conservative People's Party favour the consortium bid, leading to a growing rift in the fractious coalition government.
The conservatives have called for a special session of parliament on January 14 to discuss Europe's longest-running privatisation, now into its seventh year.
Klima refused to be pinned down on whether he would decide before the special session next Tuesday but commented: "I take it for granted that it won't take 10 days."
After the deadline of the last tender expired on December 16, the finance minister took 10 days before making public the identity of the three offers under his belt. ($1=10.90 Schilling)
